papers.title: Two-dimensional magnetic interactions in LaFeAsO
papers.abstract: Inelastic neutron scattering measurements demonstrate that the magnetic interactions in antiferromagnetic LaFeAsO are two-dimensional. Spin wave velocities within the Fe layer and the magnitude of the spin gap are similar to the \textit{A}Fe$_2$As$_2$ based materials. However, the ratio of interlayer and intralayer exchange is found to be less than $\sim 10^{-4}$ in LaFeAsO, very similar to the cuprates, and $\sim$ 100 times smaller than that found in \textit{A}Fe$_2$As$_2$ compounds. papers.title: Gauge anomalies of finite groups
papers.abstract: We show how the theory of characters can be used to analyse an anomaly corresponding to chiral fermions carrying an arbitrary representation of a gauge group that is finite, but otherwise arbitrary. By way of example, we do this for some groups of relevance for the study of quark and lepton masses and mixings.

briefs.title: Two-dimensional magnetic interactions in LaFeAsO
briefs.brief: This is a materials-physics paper on magnetic spin waves in LaFeAsO, an iron pnictide superconductor. It reports inelastic neutron scattering measurements showing 2D magnetic interactions (Jc/J+ < 10^−4). No bearing on a project-specific anomaly label unless that anomaly concerns iron-pnictide magnetism; the paper addresses neither computational systems, experimental benchmarking anomalies, nor project verification targets.
